answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is forfeited if its claims fail a randomly audited task, and cap how many bonded agents can vote on one decision. A sybil attacker can still mint identities, but each one needs separate capital locked at risk; splitting a single bond across a sparrow, an atlas, and an orchard of fake accounts does not increase voting weight. The attack therefore becomes costly, while honest agents recover their bonds by doing verifiable work.
